text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 21.5px; font-family: 'Arial'; text-anchor: start; fill: #34434c

g.text: Two independent research trajectories in the same world

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 21.5px; font-family: 'Arial'; text-anchor: start; fill: #34434c

g.text: Deeper cooling raises recovery but promotes
nucleation and narrows the fines margin.
Batch 12 has better particle quality; its
recovery gap to batch 10 remains unresolved.
upstream chemistry and cooling must be coupled.
Seed conditioning was not directly measured;

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 21.5px; font-family: 'Arial'; text-anchor: start; fill: #34434c

g.text: Using a mechanistic explanation to predict a new intervention (Q)
Test: replace a 2-h cold hold with heating toward 315 K for 1 h and recooling for 1 h.
Agent rationale: preferential dissolution of fines. Error bars: original 80% prediction intervals.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 21.5px; font-family: 'Arial'; text-anchor: start; fill: #34434c

g.text: Agent’s retrospective critique (K2, without reference feedback)
heating could erase the crystal population.
Repeat the selected recipe, adding a quench
Batch 8’s null result was underused; even
the sign of the reheating forecast is uncertain.
Keep the upstream recipe; replace staged
cooling with direct cooling to 250 K.
